spec.description: PROVIDER-API LATENCY, NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS PROVIDERS. On base-mainnet this is wallet_getCallsStatus reaching status 110 or 200. Measured live on Base: 110 does exist but fires only intermittently and trails actual Flashblock inclusion by ~0.7-1.4s (its payload carries a real blockHash one block past pendingBundle.sentAtBlock, so it denotes early BLOCK inclusion, not sub-block preconfirmation). Either way this stage lands at block-level latency (~1.7s) and does NOT measure preconfirmation. Read it as 'how long until the Wallet API will tell you' — a real user-visible number, but ~1 Base block behind actual inclusion. For cross-provider latency claims use the preconf panels instead. Pooled p50/p90/p95/p99 per region; 'samples' = attempts pooled in the window. Set range to 6h-24h.

spec.description: NEUTRAL SIGNAL — comparable across providers, and the honest counterpart to this row's canonical panel. Time from acceptance until the userOp appeared in a Base Flashblock, detected by the non-contestant newFlashblockTransactions WS oracle matching UserOperationEvent by userOpHash — the same oracle and same code path used for alchemy-mav2-bso. The gap between this and canonical is how much preconfirmation information wallet_getCallsStatus withholds from callers: status 110 exists but fires intermittently and lands ~0.7-1.4s after the Flashblock, so neither 110 nor 200 gives a caller flashblock-speed visibility. spec.description: THE APPLES-TO-APPLES COMPARISON. Every provider's preconf is measured by the same non-contestant newFlashblockTransactions WS oracle matching UserOperationEvent by userOpHash — same oracle, same code path, same clock — so rows here are directly comparable. Use this for any cross-provider or cross-modality latency claim. Do NOT use the canonical panels for that: on base-mainnet 'canonical' means different things per provider (alchemy-mav2-bso = this same Flashblock signal relabeled; alchemy-wallet-sendcalls = wallet_getCallsStatus 110/200, both of which are block-level signals ~1.7s in, since 110 trails Flashblock inclusion by ~0.7-1.4s and fires only intermittently). Check the not-observed panel before trusting these percentiles. Set range to 6h-24h.
spec.title: preconf — neutral cross-provider comparison (p50/p90/p95/p99)

spec.description: Rolling p95 (trailing 6h) for preconf AND canonical, per provider, on one axis. The preconf lines are the neutral comparison and should sit close together. Any gap between a provider's canonical line and its preconf line is observation overhead in that provider's own status API, not chain latency — for alchemy-wallet-sendcalls that gap is wallet_getCallsStatus waiting for a block-level signal — 110 when it fires, otherwise 200 — neither of which arrives at Flashblock speed.
spec.title: preconf vs canonical p95 by provider (trailing 6h)

spec.description: VALIDITY GUARD for the preconf panels. Fraction of attempts whose userOp was NOT attributed to a Flashblock. The preconf percentiles only describe the whole population while this is ~0 — if attribution degrades (schema change, WS staleness, a modality that stops emitting UserOperationEvent), the latency numbers silently become a biased fast subset. Investigate anything above a few percent before quoting preconf figures.
spec.title: preconf not-observed rate by provider

spec.description: Which signal actually ended each canonical observation, and how slow that signal is. 'attempts' shows the split — e.g. how often alchemy-wallet-sendcalls terminates on wallet_getCallsStatus 110 versus 200. Live measurement on 2026-08-06 found 110 fires on a minority of ops and still trails real Flashblock inclusion by ~0.7-1.4s, so neither row here should be read as preconfirmation; compare against the preconf panels above for that. terminal_status is populated for the canonical stage only — every other stage reports 'none', which is why this panel filters stage="canonical". Values: 110/200 (wallet_getCallsStatus), success/failure (eth_getUserOperationReceipt), none (Flashblock-sourced, no status code). Set range to 6h-24h.
spec.title: canonical by terminal_status — which signal finished, and how slow
